evals.name: capture-context-propose
evals.prompt: Design this imagined flow: prepare images and narration of a recorded session concurrently, load its recorded activity, build and save a timeline from those three inputs, derive and save a plan of intervals without identity, generate and save identified chapters from that plan, process each chapter sequentially by selecting/scoring candidate frames then synthesizing and saving its summary, summarize the session without saving, and publish the session with its processed chapters. The externally captured domain type is named Session. Timeline carries derived silences as data, and chapter planning reads those silences. Scoring is expensive and must not repeat after a synthesis failure; loading evidence and deriving candidates are cheap and may repeat. Session was captured outside this flow. Evidence preparation saves nothing. Prem takes image grids with at most four concurrent calls; OpenAI speech limits audio request size. Selection limits frames by an established budget (leave its value unspecified); the summary must cite only selected frames, regardless of the model. The implementation stores an unused timeline revision, accounts for model-call usage, retries failed synthesis with a 1000 ms delay and a backoff of two, falls back to a template for invalid summaries, and waits for human approval before publishing. The synthesis retry is established, but no failure diversion has been requested. Suggest up to three mechanism experiments as opportunities. Produce only this flow.
evals.expected_output: Rules: DP1, DP2, DP3, DP4, DP5, DP6, DP7, DP8, DP9, DP10, DP11, DS1, DS2, DS3, DS5, DS6, DS7, DS8, DS9, DS10, RE2, RE4. A coherent evidence/chapters/publication package normalized from the supplied proposal, without copying reference deviations. Reference deviations, not targets: evidence and chapters both extract images; InvalidSummary is undeclared; ChapterPolicy, loadPolicy and PlanId may be invented; GenerateChapters constructs chapters with a map in application. Keep fixtures verbatim except for requested corrections.
expectations: DP1/DP3/DS8: The package is split by shared vocabulary into multiple contexts with at least two use cases each; Session belongs to the first reader evidence and is exposed as SessionDTO; the main saga is hosted in publication.
DP2: BuildTimeline saves and returns its result as a command; PrepareImages, PrepareNarration, LoadActivity and SummarizeSession are queries regardless of paid models.

DP4/DP5/DP6: Each context has one directly constructor-injected repository; grids, fragment types and the provider four-call limit appear nowhere in interfaces, use cases, domain or sagas; any experimental mechanism comments are one-line Opportunity comments above repository methods, at most three in the package.

DP6/DP7: The frame budget is an established domain policy without a numeric value; summary verification belongs to the summary noun and is called after model output; timeline revision is omitted; domain computations are synchronous without repository imports, calculator/processor/rules objects or entity/value-object classifications.

DP8: BuildTimeline receives images, narration and activity as arguments and an upstream LoadActivity step is visible; use cases follow a single branch with ordered awaits, one Promise.all for independent application work where needed, no conditionals, domain algorithm bodies, retry/catch/limits, or use-case dependencies.

DP8: Planning intervals without identity and generating identified chapters are separate explicit transformations with their meanings explained; chapters are derived from the plan, not taken as initial flow inputs, and construction belongs to a chapter domain noun.

DP9: shared/dtos.ts contains only imports and direct aliases, including TimelineDTO with derived silences available as data; consumers import DTOs rather than another context directly and there is no mapping step.
DP10: Files use kebab-case and dot roles, domain nouns omit role suffixes, role types have UseCase/Repository/Saga/DTO suffixes, and variables are camelCase of their types preserving DTO.

DP11/RE2/RE4/DS10: The package has no README, unestablished policies, usage accounting, numeric retry settings, approval wait, choice, events, template fallback or catch; synthesis retry is only an established one-line saga note.

DS1/DS2/DS3/DS7: The main Markdown saga has one successful trunk, a fork/join parallel-input container and a plural map container with concurrency 1 whose neutral ProcessChapter link targets its own saga; ProcessChapter splits selection from synthesis without repeated selection.
DS5/DS6: Saga steps have resolving relative HTML links and suffix-free labels, exact command/query fills and borders, and neutral containers and sub-sagas.

DS9: One root sequence has trigger/saga/context lanes with distinct translucent boxes; the trigger requests once and receives the result, calls originate from the saga, parallel is par, map is loop, ProcessChapter unfolds in a grey rect with a named Note, and cross-context messages carry DTOs.
DP11: All imports, types and diagram links resolve; files are English, and any code normalizations are reported in the reply rather than Incoherence package markers.
